title: Prestonsburg: first seat on the Big Sandy
summary: Laid out as Preston’s Station in 1797 on the Levisa Fork, Prestonsburg became the seat of a vast new Floyd County in 1800 and was formally established in 1818.
bodyMarkdown:
[Prestonsburg](https://grokipedia.com/page/Prestonsburg,_Kentucky) sits on the [Levisa Fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levisa_Fork) of the Big Sandy, on land that was part of a 100,000-acre colonial grant to the family of Elizabeth Patton Preston. Her husband, [John Preston](/people/#john-preston-col), managed the grant on her behalf. The grant was meant to open land beyond the Blue Ridge to British settlement, but French and Native resistance and a change in British policy kept it from doing much for decades.

No one settled the tract until [John Spurlock](/people/#john-spurlock) of Montgomery County, Virginia, arrived in 1791. He laid out the town of Preston’s Station in 1797. The Kentucky Secretary of State’s city record says the name was later changed to honor Col. John Preston, the landowner.

On December 13, 1799, the General Assembly created [Floyd County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd_County,_Kentucky), effective June 1, 1800, from parts of Fleming, Montgomery and Mason counties. It was named for the surveyor [John Floyd](/stories/john-floyd/), and Preston’s Station became its seat.

On April 8, 1808, the first courthouse burned and took the early records with it, so Floyd County’s surviving government records begin in 1808. The post office was called Floyd Court House from 1816 until the late 1820s. The town itself was formally established in 1818.

Some popular histories credit a surveyor named John Graham with the 1797 plat and give a May 3, 1797 date. The sources checked here name John Spurlock and give no day, so this story leaves both points open.

## Kentucky today

Prestonsburg is still the Floyd County seat. The [Samuel May House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_May_House), built in 1817 and now owned by the city, is the Big Sandy Valley’s oldest known brick home, and Confederate units recruited there in the Civil War. Nearby [Middle Creek](https://grokipedia.com/page/Battle_of_Middle_Creek) was the largest Civil War battle in eastern Kentucky, fought January 10, 1862.
